title: Project Overview & Roles
description: Understand the GEC Hackathon 2026 problem, the prototype boundaries and the end-to-end safety response.
fact: Factory monitoring assistant, not an autonomous safety-certified controller.

lessons.title: The industrial safety problem
lessons.summary: Factories may experience PPE non-compliance, smoke, fire and unsafe access. Human observation can miss events or delay escalation.
lessons.action: Describe a missed-helmet scenario; identify the worker, camera, zone and responsible safety officer.
lessons.verify: Point to the corresponding hazard and response capability in the prototype.
lessons.viva: Why does a monitoring prototype need human review? → A model observation is not a confirmed hazard.

lessons.title: Project objectives
lessons.summary: The hackathon calls for factory, zone, device, worker and incident records; selected hazard identification; timestamped events; and an acknowledgement workflow.
lessons.action: Map each objective to a visible page or database concept.
lessons.verify: Distinguish implemented interfaces from aspirational integrations.
lessons.viva: What does success mean? → Traceable observation and a usable operator response workflow.

lessons.title: Factories, zones and devices
lessons.summary: A factory contains zones and monitoring devices; each camera source belongs to an operational context.
lessons.action: Sketch Factory → Zone → Camera, then connect a detection to its location.
lessons.verify: A new incident should retain location and source context.
lessons.viva: Why is the zone important? → It identifies where action is required.

lessons.title: Workers and tracking
lessons.summary: Tracking associates person detections across nearby frames; it does not establish a legal identity or reliably count unique employees across recordings.
lessons.action: Show an annotated preview if a compatible person model is active.
lessons.verify: Explain that a transient tracking ID is not proof of employee identity.
lessons.viva: Is tracking facial recognition? → No, not by itself.

lessons.title: Users and responsibilities
lessons.summary: Admin configures the system; Operator monitors and acknowledges; Safety Officer manages policies and safety workflows; Supervisor handles assigned investigations within authorized views.
lessons.action: Sign in with permitted demonstration accounts and compare accessible pages.
lessons.verify: Check backend permissions as well as hidden menu items.
lessons.viva: Why RBAC? → It limits sensitive actions and reduces unauthorized changes.

lessons.title: Detection versus incident
lessons.summary: A YOLO prediction has a class and confidence; an incident is a separate recorded workflow event when eligibility rules are met.
lessons.action: Trace sample input → filtered detection → rule evaluation → incident → acknowledgement.
lessons.verify: Never describe every bounding box as an incident.
lessons.viva: Is a detection proof of a violation? → No; rules and human verification matter.

lessons.title: Alert and response lifecycle
lessons.summary: A qualifying event can be recorded, surfaced to operators, acknowledged, assigned, investigated and resolved with audit history.
lessons.action: Walk through a test or permitted recorded event and identify decision points.
lessons.verify: Show source, severity, time, status and evidence where present.
lessons.viva: Why record acknowledgement? → To show somebody received responsibility for a report.

lessons.title: Live, uploaded and synthetic sources
lessons.summary: LIVE_CAMERA observations, UPLOADED_SAMPLE image results and SIMULATION_SENSOR TEST incidents must be interpreted separately.
lessons.action: Compare the source label in each workflow.
lessons.verify: Uploaded image/video results are not automatically saved as live incidents.
lessons.viva: Can test data be called real factory evidence? → No.

lessons.title: Prototype limitations
lessons.summary: The available project context describes a 26-check catalog with limited approved model coverage; field performance and certified use are not established.
lessons.action: Explain supported checks versus placeholders or unregistered candidate models.
lessons.verify: Do not claim 26 trained detectors or industrial certification.
lessons.viva: What is the limitation? → Coverage and real-world validation remain incomplete.

lessons.title: One-minute project viva
lessons.summary: Present problem, architecture, monitoring, incident workflow, analytics and lab testing in a coherent sequence.
lessons.action: Give a 60-second walkthrough: inputs, AI checks, event handling, human decision and reporting.
lessons.verify: State which readings and images are synthetic or demonstration-only.
lessons.viva: What is SafetyGuard AI? → A factory hazard-monitoring and response prototype.

title: Camera Network & Live Monitoring
description: Configure webcams/IP cameras, select safety policies and understand what the live annotated preview actually means.
fact: Webcam indices 0–16 and HTTP/HTTPS/RTSP sources were described in the operational workflow.

lessons.title: Camera Network page
lessons.summary: The network registers devices and associates a source with a factory or zone. Multiple cameras can have independent checklists.
lessons.action: Open Camera Network, choose a camera and review its name, type, source and zone.
lessons.verify: Show which policy belongs to that exact camera.
lessons.viva: Do all cameras share one policy? → No, policies are per camera.

lessons.title: Webcam index selection
lessons.summary: A locally connected webcam is opened by a numeric index; documented indices span 0 through 16. Index 0 is often built-in, but device assignment varies.
lessons.action: Test the candidate index while no conflicting application is holding the device.
lessons.verify: Show a legitimate frame before treating a camera as connected.
lessons.viva: Is webcam 0 always external? → No.

lessons.title: IP camera address
lessons.summary: An external network camera can use a supported HTTP, HTTPS or RTSP URL, subject to codecs, credentials, connectivity and authorization.
lessons.action: Enter the full authorized stream URL without exposing passwords in a demo.
lessons.verify: Test that the stream decodes; network reachability alone is insufficient.
lessons.viva: Why can RTSP fail? → URL, network, permissions or decoder issues.

lessons.title: Camera-to-zone assignment
lessons.summary: The selected physical zone supplies operational context for incidents and restricted-area rules.
lessons.action: Select the camera's monitored zone and save its configuration.
lessons.verify: Review the incident location to confirm the intended zone.
lessons.viva: Why store a camera zone? → To route and understand alerts.

lessons.title: Per-camera safety checks
lessons.summary: A policy selects only the checks relevant to the location; a detector must be loaded and mapped to the requested class.
lessons.action: Enable one supported check, save, and use the same camera in Live Monitoring.
lessons.verify: Confirm unselected classes are not promoted into chosen-check violations.
lessons.viva: Does selecting a check guarantee inference? → No, compatible model support is needed.

lessons.title: Start and stop streams
lessons.summary: Starting opens capture and monitoring; stopping should release that stream and end its active processing.
lessons.action: Start one authorized source, show live frames, stop it and observe the state change.
lessons.verify: Check camera status before drawing conclusions about missed events.
lessons.viva: Why stop explicitly? → To release device and compute resources.

lessons.title: Preview and inference pipeline
lessons.summary: Capture retrieves frames, OpenCV decodes, supported YOLO models infer classes, rules filter observations, and the UI renders annotations.
lessons.action: Point out source feed, detection overlay, label and confidence.
lessons.verify: Preview performance may favor recent frames instead of displaying stale ones.
lessons.viva: Is every displayed frame analyzed identically? → Not necessarily under load.

lessons.title: Tracking worker observations
lessons.summary: Temporary person tracks help relate adjacent frames and can support zone entry logic; occlusion and camera transitions break continuity.
lessons.action: Show one moving person if permitted and explain the displayed track marker.
lessons.verify: Never infer legal identity from temporary IDs.
lessons.viva: Can one ID work across all cameras? → Not guaranteed.

lessons.title: When a live incident is saved
lessons.summary: A detector prediction becomes a candidate only if the selected check, event rules and relevant timing conditions agree.
lessons.action: Demonstrate an authorized qualifying event or explain recorded evidence.
lessons.verify: Confirm the incident source is associated with the active camera, not an upload.
lessons.viva: Does one image create a live event? → Only the live-event rules decide.

lessons.title: Camera viva demonstration
lessons.summary: Combine source setup, policy selection, monitoring and alert trace in one short sequence.
lessons.action: Open Camera Network → enable supported check → start stream → inspect overlay → stop.
lessons.verify: If no camera is available, use the Test Lab without claiming live-camera validation.
lessons.viva: What's the difference between camera and video lab? → Live stream versus uploaded recording.

title: AI Safety Checks & Model Intelligence
description: Separate requested safety rules from genuinely compatible model classes, predictions and verified hazards.
fact: The safety-check catalog includes 26 options; prior operational notes indicated model support for only a subset.

lessons.title: Check catalog versus detector
lessons.summary: A UI check names a desired risk, while a model checkpoint supplies actual classes. The presence of a catalog option does not prove detector availability.
lessons.action: Compare the selected check with model-registry status.
lessons.verify: Treat unsupported checks as unsupported rather than inventing boxes.
lessons.viva: Are all 26 checks trained? → No, the catalog is broader than confirmed model coverage.

lessons.title: YOLO inference concept
lessons.summary: YOLO predicts object bounding boxes, class labels and confidence scores for supported classes.
lessons.action: Show the input frame, prediction rectangles and filtered output.
lessons.verify: A score is model confidence, not calibrated probability of a true safety event.
lessons.viva: What is YOLO used for? → Visual object detection.

lessons.title: Positive PPE versus violations
lessons.summary: Detecting a helmet or vest is not equivalent to proving PPE compliance for every worker. Missing-equipment rules need appropriate negative classes or robust association logic.
lessons.action: Compare a positive Helmet label with a supported No Helmet violation label.
lessons.verify: Absence of detection alone must not establish a violation.
lessons.viva: If no helmet box appears, is the worker non-compliant? → Not necessarily.

lessons.title: Per-camera class filtering
lessons.summary: The pipeline should surface only classes mapped to active checks on the selected camera.
lessons.action: Enable a helmet-only check and compare it with a broader model's class output.
lessons.verify: Extra model classes must not silently become unauthorized violations.
lessons.viva: Why filter? → To reduce irrelevant alerts and preserve policy semantics.

lessons.title: Fire and smoke signals
lessons.summary: Fire/flame and smoke are different checks requiring compatible predictions or sensor rules; neither a colored pixel nor a generic person class is enough.
lessons.action: Explain the class mapping using example safety footage.
lessons.verify: Distinguish visual smoke detection from manually entered simulated readings.
lessons.viva: Is simulation a smoke detector? → No.

lessons.title: Confidence and thresholds
lessons.summary: The confidence value helps interpret model predictions; thresholds trade false positives against missed detections.
lessons.action: Use a hypothetical score of 0.82 only as an example, never as actual output.
lessons.verify: Report a model's displayed score only after real inference.
lessons.viva: Does high confidence equal certainty? → No.

lessons.title: Worker tracking concepts
lessons.summary: A short-lived tracker can associate a person box across frames and support temporal rules. It is not an identity registry.
lessons.action: Explain how successive person boxes relate to the same moving subject.
lessons.verify: Tracks can reset after occlusion or camera restart.
lessons.viva: Is frame count a unique-worker count? → No.

lessons.title: Temporal rules and cooldowns
lessons.summary: Some incidents require persistence across frames and a cooldown to prevent repeated alarms. Restricted-area rules have explicit three-frame and 25-second parameters in this prototype.
lessons.action: Show the state sequence observe → qualify → cooldown.
lessons.verify: Do not imply all checks use identical timing rules.
lessons.viva: Why cooldown? → To reduce duplicate event storms.

lessons.title: False positives and review
lessons.summary: Reflections, lighting, occlusions and weak model coverage can create or hide observations. Human review labels and notes support investigation.
lessons.action: Show a false-positive workflow through Incident Management.
lessons.verify: Record why an alert was dismissed instead of deleting its history.
lessons.viva: Why keep false positives? → They inform system evaluation.

lessons.title: Candidate model boundaries
lessons.summary: Face shield/apron candidate classes exist in experimental checkpoints but are not automatically registered as approved live detectors.
lessons.action: Explain the separate local inference evaluation and normal registry.
lessons.verify: Avoid claiming experimental Face Shield and Apron classes are production-ready.
lessons.viva: Can an unregistered candidate appear in Live Monitoring? → Not automatically.

title: Incident Management & Supervisor Workflow
description: Understand incident creation, evidence, acknowledgement, assignment, false positives, escalation and closure.
fact: Incidents carry source, type, severity, time, status and relevant evidence or event history.

lessons.title: Incident record anatomy
lessons.summary: An incident is the durable object representing a candidate safety event and its handling lifecycle.
lessons.action: Open an incident record and identify ID, type, source, severity, camera/zone and timestamps.
lessons.verify: Verify the visible record is not just a transient bounding box.
lessons.viva: Which fields make an alert actionable? → What, where, when and current status.

lessons.title: Creation and evidence
lessons.summary: Eligible live rules can save incidents and evidence; simulated sensor rules save clearly marked TEST incidents. Uploaded-image and video lab inference does not save live incidents.
lessons.action: Compare a live sample record with a SIMULATION_SENSOR record.
lessons.verify: Verify every sample is correctly labeled.
lessons.viva: Does Image Lab add incident evidence? → Not automatically.

lessons.title: Alert presentation
lessons.summary: Dashboard notices, browser/audio prompts and configured email channels may surface a recorded event, but they are distinct mechanisms.
lessons.action: Show an active alert indicator and, where permitted, corresponding notification settings.
lessons.verify: A recorded incident does not guarantee every delivery channel succeeded.
lessons.viva: What if email fails? → The incident record remains separate from delivery.

lessons.title: Acknowledgement
lessons.summary: An authorized operator or safety responder acknowledges awareness of a reported incident. Acknowledgement is not the same as fixing the hazard.
lessons.action: Open a pending incident and use the permitted acknowledge action.
lessons.verify: Observe user and timestamp in status/history where surfaced.
lessons.viva: Is acknowledgement resolution? → No.

lessons.title: Supervisor assignment
lessons.summary: Assigned supervisors can investigate events in their authorized scope, rather than gaining unrestricted access to all configuration.
lessons.action: Assign or inspect an assigned supervisor from the permitted administrative view.
lessons.verify: Verify role permissions in the interface and backend.
lessons.viva: Why assign an owner? → To make follow-up responsibility explicit.

lessons.title: False-positive decisions
lessons.summary: A model can misclassify scenes; an authorized reviewer can mark a report false positive and preserve an audit trail.
lessons.action: Use a documented example and explain the reason for dismissal.
lessons.verify: Keep original source and decision history for later quality analysis.
lessons.viva: Why not simply delete it? → Auditability and model improvement.

lessons.title: Escalation and timeouts
lessons.summary: An overdue serious report can qualify for escalation based on enabled rules. The documented default is HIGH+ after 120 seconds.
lessons.action: Show settings and explain what happens when an incident remains unacknowledged.
lessons.verify: Treat delivery as separately observable from eligibility.
lessons.viva: What causes escalation? → Configured severity and delay with no timely acknowledgement.

lessons.title: Investigation notes
lessons.summary: Evidence, findings, probable cause and corrective actions can be recorded as investigation notes by authorized people.
lessons.action: Demonstrate a concise note such as 'reviewed PPE footage; retraining recommended'.
lessons.verify: Distinguish factual observation from unverified conclusion.
lessons.viva: Why store notes? → To document reasoning and actions.

lessons.title: Resolution and closure
lessons.summary: Resolution records the authorized decision that work on an incident is complete. Its audit trail can show prior acknowledgement, assignment and review.
lessons.action: Open a handled incident and explain its status chronology.
lessons.verify: Never equate closing the ticket with certified removal of physical risk.
lessons.viva: What does resolved mean? → Workflow completion, subject to real-world verification.

lessons.title: Incident viva walkthrough
lessons.summary: Trace one sample case from detection to response and audit, optionally using a TEST synthetic incident if no camera is available.
lessons.action: Create a legitimate demo event → locate incident → acknowledge → assign/review → add notes → resolve.
lessons.verify: State explicitly whether each step is live, sample, or simulated.
lessons.viva: What makes it end-to-end? → Event, response, accountability and evidence.

title: Analytics, Reports & Safety Intelligence
description: Interpret incident trends, severity, locations, false positives and response times without overstating the data.
fact: Analytics describe stored records. They cannot validate a model or the factory safety state by themselves.

lessons.title: Dashboard KPIs
lessons.summary: Overview cards summarize stored incidents, unresolved workload, severity and recent activity according to current filters.
lessons.action: Open Analytics and compare a displayed metric with filtered incident records.
lessons.verify: Check that TEST data and date range are understood.
lessons.viva: Can a high incident count mean improved detection? → Possibly; context matters.

lessons.title: Time-series trends
lessons.summary: Time-bucketed incident charts help reveal when recorded hazard observations increased or decreased.
lessons.action: Select a date window and compare daily or weekly bins where available.
lessons.verify: Interpret trends as counts of records, not independently verified factory accident rates.
lessons.viva: What is the x-axis? → Time interval.

lessons.title: Severity breakdown
lessons.summary: A severity chart groups incidents by severity class.
lessons.action: Inspect counts for high, medium, low and TEST where applicable.
lessons.verify: Do not merge TEST events with confirmed industrial severity without disclosure.
lessons.viva: Why severity? → To prioritize response.

lessons.title: Camera-level activity
lessons.summary: Per-camera counts can reveal noisy scenes or repeatedly triggered policies.
lessons.action: Choose a camera and identify its reported events for a timeframe.
lessons.verify: Normalize by monitoring duration before comparing camera risk.
lessons.viva: Can camera A's higher count prove it is less safe? → No.

lessons.title: Zone and hazard analysis
lessons.summary: Location and incident-type breakdowns help identify where and what is frequently reported.
lessons.action: Filter by zone, hazard type and incident source.
lessons.verify: Verify missing or unmapped zones are not mistaken for safe locations.
lessons.viva: What is a hotspot? → An area with relatively concentrated recorded events.

lessons.title: False-positive rate
lessons.summary: A useful review metric is dismissed false-positive reports divided by evaluated incidents, with denominator clearly defined.
lessons.action: Explain the calculation using a hypothetical 4 false positives among 20 reviewed incidents = 20%.
lessons.verify: Do not report a denominator as total frames or all unreviewed events.
lessons.viva: Does 20% measure model precision? → Not directly.

lessons.title: Response-time metrics
lessons.summary: Response duration is commonly measured from incident creation to acknowledgement; reporting rules must handle unacknowledged records.
lessons.action: Compute an illustrative 10:00 → 10:03 acknowledgement as 3 minutes.
lessons.verify: Clarify whether average includes only acknowledged incidents.
lessons.viva: What does MTT A mean? → Mean time to acknowledgement.

lessons.title: Source segmentation
lessons.summary: LIVE_CAMERA records, synthetic TEST sensor records and image/video lab results belong to different evidentiary categories.
lessons.action: Filter or explain groups by source and severity.
lessons.verify: Uploaded media analysis does not create ordinary incident rows.
lessons.viva: Why separate simulated events? → To prevent distorted operational conclusions.

lessons.title: CSV and evidence review
lessons.summary: A report export helps review records in Excel and attach supporting analysis to a hackathon presentation.
lessons.action: Export where available and inspect IDs, times, types, statuses and filters.
lessons.verify: Remove workplace personal data before public sharing.
lessons.viva: Are charts a replacement for row-level audit? → No.

lessons.title: Analytics viva walkthrough
lessons.summary: Show overview, date trend, severity, camera activity, false-positive review, response time and source separation.
lessons.action: Explain one chart with a real record from the demo database.
lessons.verify: Do not invent numbers: show the current system output or label examples hypothetical.
lessons.viva: What's the most important caveat? → Metrics reflect collected and classified data.

title: Settings, Zones & Escalation Rules
description: Configure restricted-area geometry, rule eligibility, alerts, diagnostics and permissions.
fact: Restricted-area logic uses normalized polygons, person-box foot points and temporal safeguards.

lessons.title: Roles and setting scope
lessons.summary: System-wide configuration changes require elevated access; operators generally observe and respond rather than rewiring safety policies.
lessons.action: Compare authorized Admin/Safety Officer controls with Operator and Supervisor views.
lessons.verify: Hidden buttons do not replace backend authorization.
lessons.viva: Who should change policy? → An explicitly authorized configuration role.

lessons.title: Draw a restricted polygon
lessons.summary: A selected camera can have a restricted-area polygon made of 3–12 normalized points.
lessons.action: Use a frame preview to place a closed boundary around the prohibited zone.
lessons.verify: Avoid self-intersecting or tiny polygons and save with the correct camera.
lessons.viva: Why minimum three points? → A planar polygon needs at least three vertices.

lessons.title: Normalized coordinates
lessons.summary: Coordinates are stored proportionally to image dimensions, allowing geometry to scale as the preview resolution changes.
lessons.action: Explain x = pixel_x/frame_width and y = pixel_y/frame_height.
lessons.verify: Ensure all saved coordinates map to the intended part of the camera view.
lessons.viva: Why normalize? → To avoid resolution-specific geometry.

lessons.title: Person foot-point test
lessons.summary: For restricted-zone entry, the system evaluates the bottom-center of a detected person box rather than simply testing any box overlap.
lessons.action: Draw the person box and mark its lower-center point in the diagram.
lessons.verify: A partial body overlap should not be described as a confirmed entry by itself.
lessons.viva: Why bottom-center? → It approximates ground contact.

lessons.title: Restricted event timing
lessons.summary: The documented geofence rule requires three consecutive qualifying frames and a 25-second cooldown before a repeated incident.
lessons.action: Explain the sequence: track enters → persists → event → cooldown.
lessons.verify: Point out that these exact settings apply to this rule, not every hazard.
lessons.viva: Why 3 frames? → To reduce one-frame noise.

lessons.title: Camera-specific enablement
lessons.summary: A polygon alone is not sufficient if the relevant RESTRICTED_ZONE check is not enabled for that camera.
lessons.action: Enable the matching check, assign the polygon and test with authorized material.
lessons.verify: Verify the geometry and selected policy correspond to the same source.
lessons.viva: Why must both be enabled? → Detection requires policy plus zone configuration.

lessons.title: Escalation defaults
lessons.summary: Operational context describes escalation as enabled, eligible at HIGH and above after 120 seconds, subject to installed configuration.
lessons.action: Show severity selector, timeout and escalation enable flag.
lessons.verify: Describe it as a configurable workflow rule, not guaranteed external delivery.
lessons.viva: Does every LOW alert escalate? → Not under the stated default.

lessons.title: Notification channels
lessons.summary: In-app dashboard, audio, browser and email channels have different dependencies and delivery semantics.
lessons.action: Check each enabled channel and demonstrate the locally supported one.
lessons.verify: Do not claim an email was received unless delivery is verified.
lessons.viva: Why separate channels? → One may fail while records still exist.

lessons.title: System diagnostics and retention
lessons.summary: Diagnostics help distinguish camera connectivity, model loading, queue health, logs and stored media retention.
lessons.action: Check model registry, camera status, backend health and retained output.
lessons.verify: Remove test media according to the site's retention policy; do not expose raw worker footage.
lessons.viva: What do diagnostics prove? → System status, not detector accuracy.

lessons.title: Settings viva walkthrough
lessons.summary: Create and review one camera-restricted polygon and explain alert escalation, then restore safe demo settings.
lessons.action: Show polygon points → enable check → explain foot-point → 3 frames → cooldown → escalate if unresolved.
lessons.verify: Use illustrations if no authorized footage is available.
lessons.viva: What could go wrong? → Incorrect geometry, policy or detector support.

title: Architecture, Database & APIs
description: Explain how input, inference, business rules, storage, authentication, evidence and reporting are connected.
fact: Project components referenced previously include FastAPI, OpenCV, Ultralytics YOLO, Python tracking and SQLite.

lessons.title: End-to-end architecture
lessons.summary: Camera or uploaded media enters the Python server; OpenCV decodes frames; models predict; rules evaluate; approved events reach SQLite and UI endpoints.
lessons.action: Trace Input → Inference → Policy → Event → Database → Interface.
lessons.verify: Keep asynchronous notification work separate from the incident decision.
lessons.viva: Why use layers? → To isolate processing, rules and presentation.

lessons.title: API and session protection
lessons.summary: The web frontend communicates with authenticated Python HTTP endpoints. Role checks should be enforced server-side for privileged actions.
lessons.action: Explain request → authentication → authorization → handler → response.
lessons.verify: Do not mistake login UI visibility for API security.
lessons.viva: Why authenticate the endpoint? → To protect media, incidents and settings.

lessons.title: Camera capture services
lessons.summary: OpenCV capture connects to a selected index or stream URL and converts decoded frames into images for inference.
lessons.action: Explain start, read, fail/reconnect and stop lifecycle.
lessons.verify: Invalid stream URLs must not generate fictitious live detections.
lessons.viva: Why isolate capture? → Different cameras and codecs can fail independently.

lessons.title: Model registry and check mapping
lessons.summary: A model registry records checkpoints and class mappings; safety-check filtering decides which classes a selected policy may use.
lessons.action: Trace a MISSING_HELMET check to a compatible model class.
lessons.verify: A declared catalog option does not create missing trained weights.
lessons.viva: What prevents fabricated results? → Registered compatibility and actual inference.

lessons.title: Safety rules and temporal logic
lessons.summary: Hazard rules convert compatible model observations into possible incidents using configured policy, region and persistence conditions.
lessons.action: Explain how a restricted-zone rule combines tracker, polygon, 3 frames and cooldown.
lessons.verify: Keep thresholds specific to their originating rule.
lessons.viva: Why not save every frame? → It would create duplicate unreviewed alarms.

lessons.title: SQLite entity design
lessons.summary: The previously discussed database includes devices, policies, incidents, evidence, events, supervisors, restricted areas, escalation and outbox records.
lessons.action: Sketch relationships: Device → Incidents → Evidence/Events; Supervisor ← Assignments.
lessons.verify: Exact column names require the repository schema; do not invent SQL DDL.
lessons.viva: Why separate incident events? → Audit history needs multiple actions per record.

lessons.title: Evidence and audit trail
lessons.summary: A qualifying live event may store time-stamped evidence, while a user action appends an auditable workflow change.
lessons.action: Explain who performed what action, to which incident and when.
lessons.verify: Check retention and access control for media containing workers.
lessons.viva: Why preserve history? → Accountability and later investigation.

lessons.title: Image analysis API
lessons.summary: The implemented image-lab endpoint is POST /api/images/analyze; it validates uploaded media, runs supported checks and returns annotated sample output.
lessons.action: Review fields source=UPLOADED_SAMPLE and saved_as_incident=false.
lessons.verify: Never call returned sample predictions live event records.
lessons.viva: Does this endpoint alert the factory? → No.

lessons.title: Offline job and sensor APIs
lessons.summary: Offline video jobs are processed from stored uploads; POST /api/sensors/simulate tests numeric rules and can create TEST records.
lessons.action: Contrast a media job with a synchronous synthetic reading and its incident IDs.
lessons.verify: Video owner-scoping, job IDs and queue limits protect processing.
lessons.viva: How many concurrent video inferences? → One job executes at a time in the cited implementation.

lessons.title: Architecture viva walkthrough
lessons.summary: Explain the major services and connect each one to a visible user action.
lessons.action: Demonstrate a sample image analysis, then trace a simulated TEST incident into the database-facing UI.
lessons.verify: State that deployment, scalability and certification are separate future engineering tasks.
lessons.viva: Why is it a prototype? → It demonstrates a workflow without validated industrial reliability.

title: AI Test Lab: Image, Video & Sensors
description: A hands-on guide to single-image predictions, offline annotated MP4, synthetic sensor thresholds and viva demonstrations.
fact: Image/video lab outputs are unconfirmed and not live incidents; sensor experiments create explicitly labeled TEST incidents.

lessons.title: What the Lab tests
lessons.summary: Image Lab evaluates one sample photograph; Video Lab processes a recording; Sensor Lab applies numeric test thresholds. These are separate experimental workflows.
lessons.action: Open AI Test Lab and identify its three sections.
lessons.verify: Image/video use supported YOLO inference, sensor simulation does not.
lessons.viva: Can this replace factory validation? → No.

lessons.title: Image formats and limits
lessons.summary: Valid image uploads accept JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 8 MB and 24 megapixels; wide images are resized to 1280 pixels and inference runs at size 640.
lessons.action: Choose an authorized PPE photo, check extension and upload size.
lessons.verify: The backend decodes actual image content; renaming a bad file is insufficient.
lessons.viva: What output appears? → Annotated JPEG and detection data.

lessons.title: Image prediction workflow
lessons.summary: Select Camera 1 and a supported check such as MISSING_HELMET, save the camera policy, then click Analyze photo.
lessons.action: Identify predicted label, bounding box, confidence, chosen checks and potential violations.
lessons.verify: Missing detections do not prove compliance; no actual score is predetermined.
lessons.viva: Is confidence a safety guarantee? → No.

lessons.title: Image endpoint and response
lessons.summary: POST /api/images/analyze validates and decodes, selects compatible models, filters classes and returns a Base64 JPEG with a sample-analysis warning.
lessons.action: Read the sample-response fields UPLOADED_SAMPLE and saved_as_incident=false.
lessons.verify: Confirm no central incident or notification is created by this image test.
lessons.viva: Why no incident? → It is controlled offline inference.

lessons.title: Choose supported checks
lessons.summary: Camera policy limits the labels that can be reported; only registered compatible model classes should be considered. Experimental face-shield/apron candidate weights are not automatically approved.
lessons.action: Compare a helmet-only selection with the model class list.
lessons.verify: Do not claim all catalog checks have working trained detectors.
lessons.viva: What if no detector is usable? → Show the compatibility problem, not a false prediction.

lessons.title: Video formats and limits
lessons.summary: The offline lab accepts MP4, MOV, AVI, MKV or WebM, up to 350 MB and 20 minutes, depending on decode support. Standard H.264 MP4 is a practical demo choice.
lessons.action: Prepare a short authorized clip, check its codec and use the selected camera checks or saved independent checklist.
lessons.verify: A supported extension does not guarantee decoder compatibility.
lessons.viva: What gets generated? → Annotated MP4 when the job succeeds.

lessons.title: Video processing job
lessons.summary: Video upload creates a queued job; OpenCV decodes frames, YOLO predicts supported classes, annotations are drawn and a new MP4 is encoded.
lessons.action: Track job status queued → processing → completed/failed, frame progress and class counts.
lessons.verify: Only one offline inference job executes at once; the queue admits up to three active/queued jobs.
lessons.viva: What does progress mean? → Frames processed, not percent of safety achieved.

lessons.title: Understand video outputs
lessons.summary: Annotated footage distinguishes PRESENT (green), VIOLATION (red) and REVIEW (amber), with an UNCONFIRMED MODEL DETECTIONS overlay. Successful runs offer preview and download.
lessons.action: Show the saved MP4 and explain detections across frames.
lessons.verify: Forty-five missing-helmet detections may come from one repeatedly observed person.
lessons.viva: Are frame counts unique incidents? → No.

lessons.title: Synthetic smoke and heat
lessons.summary: An authorized Admin or Safety Officer enters manual values. Smoke >=300 ppm creates SMOKE TEST; temperature >=70°C creates HIGH_TEMPERATURE TEST. These are prototype thresholds, not approved industrial limits.
lessons.action: Try 100 ppm/30°C (none), 350/35 (SMOKE) and 100/80 (HIGH_TEMPERATURE).
lessons.verify: Check source=SIMULATION_SENSOR and severity=TEST in Incidents.
lessons.viva: Is a physical sensor connected? → No.

lessons.title: Security and complete lab viva
lessons.summary: Lab access is authenticated. Main UI provides Image/Video to Admin, Operator and Safety Officer; synthetic reading and policy change to Admin/Safety Officer. Some upload API role checks need tightening.
lessons.action: Demonstrate image → optional short video → synthetic below threshold → synthetic above threshold → inspect TEST record.
lessons.verify: Owner-scoped video files, valid upload bounds, proper retention and backend RBAC must be discussed.
lessons.viva: What is the central distinction? → Uploaded media tests models; synthetic readings test event recording.
